MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Requisition ID: REQ677142
Employment Type: Permanent Part - Time
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Specialist - Grade 2
Remuneration: $128,301.89 - $132,523.13 per annum, pro rata (+ super + 17.5% leave loading where applicable) 
Hours per week:16 
Applications Close: 4 August 2026 
Vaccination Category: A
Located in: Wagga Wagga

Lead When It Matters Most. Be the Calm in Every Emergency

About the Opportunity-
Join the Wagga Wagga Base Hospital After Hours team as a Clinical Nurse Specialist Grade 2 - After Hours Clinical Support and play a vital role in supporting staff and responding to clinical emergencies across the hospital.
Working after hours, you'll provide advanced clinical support, leadership and expert decision-making to nursing and multidisciplinary teams, ensuring safe, timely and high-quality care when senior clinical support is needed most. You'll respond to deteriorating patients, cardiac arrests and medical emergencies, assisting Team Leaders with advanced life support, defibrillation, emergency medication administration and airway, breathing and circulation management.
This autonomous and highly respected role requires advanced clinical judgement, excellent communication skills and the confidence to lead and support staff in complex situations. You'll also mentor nurses, promote evidence-based practice and contribute to a culture of continuous learning, safety and clinical excellence.

About You
Our ideal candidate will have:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA.

Clinical Nurse Specialist Grade 2 qualifications with relevant postgraduate qualifications and at least three years' experience in an acute specialty. 

Current Advanced Life Support (ALS2) certification with demonstrated competence in emergency response, including defibrillation, emergency medications and advanced assessment of airway, breathing and circulation. 

Demonstrated experience managing deteriorating patients and supporting Team Leaders during medical emergencies and cardiac arrests. 

Advanced clinical assessment, critical thinking and decision-making skills with the ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced acute hospital environment. 

Proven leadership, mentoring and communication skills with the ability to support and educate nursing staff while working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams. 

Commitment to evidence-based practice, patient safety, quality improvement and ongoing professional development.

As the Clinical Nurse Consultant, you will:

Demonstrate advanced clinical assessment, decision-making and consultation skills. 

Have the ability to support clinicians through virtual care platforms and complex patient flow processes. 

Be confident coordinating interfacility transfers and navigating competing clinical priorities.

Demonstrate strong leadership, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. 

Be committed to evidence-based practice, quality improvement and service development. 

Thrive in a collaborative multidisciplinary environment and contribute to education, mentoring and capability building across the District.
 

To find out more, please review the Position Description

About You
Our ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Current registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse.

Have minimum 3 years post-registration nursing experience, including at least 3 years recent experience within a critical care environment.

Completion of a Graduate Nurse Program or equivalent

Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.

A strong commitment to person-centred care, cultural safety, and ongoing professional development.

Why join MLHD?

At Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), we offer more than a job - we offer the chance to make a real difference.

Meaningful Impact - Play a vital role in supporting essential services to our diverse and vibrant regional communities.

Flexible Working Arrangements - Designed to support work-life balance, aligned with NSW Health policy. 

Generous Salary Packaging - Access up to $20,600 per annum tax-free for living expenses, plus the option for novated car leasing.

Professional Development - Take advantage of ongoing learning and career development opportunities.

Health & Wellbeing Support - Benefit from our comprehensive wellness programs for you and your family, including Employee Assistance Programs Fitness Passport and initiatives to support both physical and mental health.

Click here to discover why MLHD is the right place to grow your career and contribute to healthier communities.

How to Apply
If this sounds like the opportunity for you, click apply now! Please contact Verina Walsh, via Verina.Walsh@health.nsw.gov.au if you have any questions about this role.
Your application will need to include:

A current CV

A cover letter

Responses to the application questions

MLHD welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and is committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. 
We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disability, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and the LGBTIQ+ community. 
If you identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, you can access recruitment application support through the Stepping Up initiative.

This is a NSW Health Category A position which requires immunisation and screening for certain diseases. The full list of requirements are outlined in the NSW Health OASV Policy (Page 11). You will be required to complete the OASV Undertaking- Declaration Form and 

TB Assessment Tool during the recruitment process. Please upload this with your application along with any other vaccination evidence that you may have.

 As a Disability Support Worker with Oyster Care, you'll be responsible for the day-to-day care of our Participants with physical disabilities and/or mental illness. Oyster Care Support Workers enable our participants to reach their full potential by helping them achieve their individual goals. 

 Monday to Saturday:

	 Complex mental health needs 
	 Behavioural challenges

	 Mental Health experience is highly favourable but not required. 
	 Excellent work ethic, strong oral communication skills and written skills. 
	 Have an empathetic and person-centered approach when supporting our Participants in their own home and/or out in the community. Treat them how you would treat your own family member.

  Essential Criteria:  

 
	 Must be willing to travel around Sydney. 
	 Must be vaccinated for COVID-19.

The Project Support Officer is responsible for coordinating and undertaking a range of high-quality project support, administration and reporting functions across the Business Transformation portfolio of projects and digital initiatives. 

The role coordinates and undertakes project records management and reporting functions, provides a responsive point of contact service, provides advice on project administration functions and processes and develops and maintains positive working relationships with internal and external project stakeholders.

SA Health committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment)
